findings.highlight: But that would mean openly rejecting Takeya's invitation.
findings.evidenceJa:
けれど、つまりそれって、
武也の誘いと思いっきりバッティングしてるってこと。
findings.explanation: The concert directly conflicts in time with Takeya's invitation; the English says attending would openly reject Takeya.
findings.japanese:
けれど、つまりそれって、
武也の誘いと思いっきりバッティングしてるってこと。
findings.todokanai: But that would mean openly rejecting Takeya's invitation.

findings.highlight: what I'd be seeing again are memories pertaining to a certain someone
findings.evidenceJa: いや、これから集めるであろう“あいつ”のことを。
findings.explanation: Correcting himself from the previous sentence, Haruki thinks of the attention 'she'—Kazusa—will surely go on gathering from audiences in the future. The English instead says he would see memories about her again, replacing a forward-looking image of Kazusa's career with retrospective recollection.
findings.japanese: いや、これから集めるであろう“あいつ”のことを。
findings.todokanai: No, what I'd be seeing again are memories pertaining to a certain someone.

findings.highlight: I have no right to even remember the name "Touma"
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜との決着をつけないまま、“冬馬”という姓を引きずるのは。
findings.explanation: Haruki decides to stop dragging the name Touma behind him while his relationship with Setsuna remains unresolved. The English invents a moral prohibition—that he has no right even to remember the name—turning his decision to stop pursuing a connection into self-punishing memory erasure.
findings.japanese:
雪菜との決着をつけないまま、
“冬馬”という姓を引きずるのは。
findings.todokanai: I have no right to even remember the name "Touma" when I can't even have proper closure with Setsuna.

findings.highlight: "Well, I won't go if you won't tell me where you are."
findings.evidenceJa: 「じゃあ、駄目な方向で」
findings.explanation: Haruki jokingly says 'then let's make it no'; the English invents a condition about Takeya refusing to disclose his location.
findings.japanese: 「じゃあ、駄目な方向で」
findings.todokanai: "Well, I won't go if you won't tell me where you are."

findings.highlight: "You could've just said so to begin with, you know. You always get caught up in pointless conversation."
findings.evidenceJa:
「最初からそう言やいいんだよ。
余計な気、使いやがって」
findings.explanation: Haruki accuses Takeya of unnecessary consideration; the English accuses him of pointless conversation.
findings.japanese:
「最初からそう言やいいんだよ。
余計な気、使いやがって」
findings.todokanai: "You could've just said so to begin with, you know. You always get caught up in pointless conversation."

findings.highlight: just as Haruki makes his decision to be with her
findings.evidenceJa: 春希が雪菜に向かい合おうとした途端
findings.explanation: Io says Setsuna rejected Haruki at the moment he finally tried to face her honestly. The English upgrades that attempt at direct engagement into a decision to be with her, asserting a settled relationship commitment stronger than the Japanese.
findings.japanese:
「なのに、春希が雪菜に向かい合おうとした途端、
そんなわかりきってたこと持ち出して
春希の手をはねのけるって、一体どういう了見だよ！」
findings.todokanai: "But just as Haruki makes his decision to be with her, Setsuna brings up something so obvious and slaps Haruki's hand aside? What the hell is she thinking!?"

findings.highlight: Make Haruki admit that it was his fault!
findings.evidenceJa: 責めろよ！　春希の非を認めてやれよ！
findings.explanation: Io says Setsuna should have blamed Haruki and acknowledged his fault for him, giving him the condemnation he needed. The English says Setsuna should force Haruki himself to admit fault, reversing the person who must perform the acknowledgment and undermining Io's central argument.
findings.japanese:
「ギリギリになって大爆発するくらいなら
最初から弾けろよ！
責めろよ！　春希の非を認めてやれよ！」
findings.todokanai: "If she's just going to explode at the end, then she might as well point it out from the very beginning! Yell at him! Make Haruki admit that it was his fault!"

findings.highlight: Io didn't mention anything specific, and even Takeya didn't admit it openly
findings.evidenceJa: 依緒に言われるまでもなく、武也に同意されるまでもなく、俺の罪は、俺が一番よく知ってる。
findings.explanation: Haruki says that, without needing Io to tell him or Takeya to agree, he knows his own sins best. The English falsely states that Io was nonspecific and Takeya did not openly admit the truth, contradicting the explicit accusations and agreement immediately before it.
findings.japanese:
依緒に言われるまでもなく、
武也に同意されるまでもなく、
俺の罪は、俺が一番よく知ってる。
findings.todokanai: Io didn't mention anything specific, and even Takeya didn't admit it openly, but I'm the one most aware of all the sins I've committed.

findings.highlight: "It took her way too much time… In all the time she took moping around like that, Haruki never once forgot about Touma."
findings.evidenceJa:
「かかりすぎなんだよ…
そうやって雪菜がモタモタしてる間、
春希はずっと、冬馬のこと忘れられなかったんだから」
findings.explanation: Io says Setsuna dawdled; the English says she moped around.
findings.japanese:
「かかりすぎなんだよ…
そうやって雪菜がモタモタしてる間、
春希はずっと、冬馬のこと忘れられなかったんだから」
findings.todokanai: "It took her way too much time… In all the time she took moping around like that, Haruki never once forgot about Touma."

findings.highlight: That's what's forced them into this situation where they can't move on or go back, either
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜が引きずるから。引きずったまま、引きずってないふりなんかするから！
findings.explanation: Io says Setsuna keeps dragging the past with her while pretending she is not dragging it at all. The English replaces Setsuna's specific repression and pretense with a generic shared inability to move forward or back, deleting the behavior Io is condemning.
findings.japanese:
「雪菜が引きずるから。
引きずったまま、引きずってないふりなんかするから！」
findings.todokanai: "It's because Setsuna refused to let go. That's what's forced them into this situation where they can't move on or go back, either!"

findings.highlight: Maybe you were just too dense to realize it?
findings.evidenceJa: ボケんのも大概にしろよ？
findings.explanation: After Io absurdly claims she has never dumped anyone, Takeya tells her to stop playing the fool or carrying the joke too far. The English instead speculates that Io was too dense to realize she had rejected people, changing a direct angry rebuke into a diagnosis of obliviousness.
findings.japanese: 「………ボケんのも大概にしろよ？」
findings.todokanai: "…Maybe you were just too dense to realize it?"

findings.highlight: The crowd's excitement floods my surroundings as it drowns out the sound of the New Year's bell meant for the first night of the year, bringing me the slightest bit of discomfort.
findings.evidenceJa:
除夜の鐘を掻き消すような興奮が俺の周囲に蔓延して、
ほんの少しだけ居心地の悪さを感じたけれど。
findings.explanation: The joy of concertgoers drowns out the year-end temple bell; the English calls it a bell meant for the first night of the year.
findings.japanese:
除夜の鐘を掻き消すような興奮が俺の周囲に蔓延して、
ほんの少しだけ居心地の悪さを感じたけれど。
findings.todokanai: The crowd's excitement floods my surroundings as it drowns out the sound of the New Year's bell meant for the first night of the year, bringing me the slightest bit of discomfort.

findings.highlight: "Being in Japan is what makes it special. We don't often get a chance to come back like this, so I want to try heating up a pot of it the old-fashioned way."
findings.evidenceJa:
「日本でってのが重要なのよ。
せっかく帰国してるんだから、
こう、お銚子で熱燗とかさぁ」
findings.explanation: Youko wants hot sake served from a small sake flask; the English says she wants to heat a pot in an old-fashioned way.
findings.japanese:
「日本でってのが重要なのよ。
せっかく帰国してるんだから、
こう、お銚子で熱燗とかさぁ」
findings.todokanai: "Being in Japan is what makes it special. We don't often get a chance to come back like this, so I want to try heating up a pot of it the old-fashioned way."

findings.highlight: I was on the floor until just a moment ago
findings.evidenceJa: 実はさっきまでずっと下がりっぱなしだったんだよね
findings.explanation: Io says that despite drinking, her energy or mood had remained down until moments ago. The English puts her literally on the floor, inventing a physical position and missing the contrast between her earlier low spirits and her suddenly manic greeting.
findings.japanese:
「あ～、確かにさっきまで飲んでたんだけどさぁ、
実はさっきまでずっと下がりっぱなしだったんだよね」
findings.todokanai: "Aaaah, well yeah, I was drinking until just a little while ago. To be honest, I was on the floor until just a moment ago."

findings.highlight: Now all that's left is for you two to say it to each other, right?
findings.evidenceJa: あけましておめでとう、武也、依緒。…お前らにだけ挨拶まだだったよな？
findings.explanation: Haruki greets Takeya and Io and jokes that they were the only people he had not yet wished a happy new year. The English instead tells them that they still need to greet each other, changing his cheeky recovery after the confession and disrupting their immediate mock assault on him.
findings.japanese:
「あけましておめでとう、武也、依緒。
…お前らにだけ挨拶まだだったよな？」
findings.todokanai: "Happy New Year, Takeya, Io. …Now all that's left is for you two to say it to each other, right?"

findings.highlight: she's such a waste on you
findings.evidenceJa: ほんとお前、ホント勿体ぶりやがって！
findings.explanation: Takeya complains that Haruki dragged out the revelation and made them wait in suspense. The English invents a judgment that Setsuna is wasted on Haruki, changing both the referent and the reason for Takeya's exasperation.
findings.japanese:
「くっそ、今日は朝まで付き合えよ？
ほんとお前、ホント勿体ぶりやがって！」
findings.todokanai: "Screw it all, we'll be drinking until morning now, got it? Man, she's such a waste on you!"

findings.highlight: …If anything, they're probably enjoying the sight of us, who were in a quarrel just a moment ago, get along.
findings.evidenceJa:
…さっきまで喧嘩してたはずの俺たちの、
あまりに仲良しな光景にあてられつつも。
findings.explanation: Bystanders may be overwhelmed or put off by the trio's excessively close display; the English says they are probably enjoying it.
findings.japanese:
…さっきまで喧嘩してたはずの俺たちの、
あまりに仲良しな光景にあてられつつも。
findings.todokanai: …If anything, they're probably enjoying the sight of us, who were in a quarrel just a moment ago, get along.

findings.highlight: the reliable ones who supported me, to the not-so-reliable ones who supported me, and to those who supported me even when asked not to
findings.evidenceJa: 頼もしく自分を支えてくれる人に。頼んでもいないのに支えようとする人に。嫌だと言っても支えられようとする人に。
findings.explanation: The source distinguishes a reliable person who supports Haruki, someone who tries to support him unasked, and someone who tries to be supported by him despite saying she does not want it. The English calls the second group unreliable without basis and turns the third passive relationship into yet another person actively supporting Haruki, flattening the carefully varied network of dependence.
findings.japanese:
頼もしく自分を支えてくれる人に。
頼んでもいないのに支えようとする人に。
嫌だと言っても支えられようとする人に。
findings.todokanai: Here's to the reliable ones who supported me, to the not-so-reliable ones who supported me, and to those who supported me even when asked not to.

findings.highlight: And to the one most beloved person who stayed by my side, despite all the grief I put her through…
findings.evidenceJa:
そして、いつも近くにいたのに、
ずっと、悲しませてばかりだった大切な人に…
findings.explanation: Setsuna is Haruki's important person; the English adds the superlative 'most beloved.'
findings.japanese:
そして、いつも近くにいたのに、
ずっと、悲しませてばかりだった大切な人に…
findings.todokanai: And to the one most beloved person who stayed by my side, despite all the grief I put her through…

findings.highlight: I hope it'll be a great year indeed
findings.evidenceJa: 願わくは、今年“から”はいい年でありますように。
findings.explanation: The marked から means Haruki hopes that from this year onward things will finally be good, explicitly contrasting the future with the years of damage behind them. The English drops 'from' and its typographic emphasis, reducing the closing turn to an ordinary new-year wish.
findings.japanese:
願わくは、今年“から”は
いい年でありますように。
findings.todokanai: And I hope it'll be a great year indeed.
